title: Independent Retail Pharmacy Facility Directory
demand_signal: Strong and validated, with a transparent commercial market and a clear niche-vendor anchor. NCPA (National Community Pharmacists Association) reports ~19,400 independent community pharmacies in the US, an addressable segment that is repeatedly packaged and resold by vendors. Active commercial vendors selling pharmacy FACILITY (not pharmacist) lists at premium pricing: LeadsPlease (US Independent Pharmacy lists), FrescoData ('60K+ pharmacy locations' database), HealthcareMailing ('Pharmacy Email List', 90K+ records), MedicoLeads (pharmacy database with NABP/DEA enrichment), BookYourData (retail pharmacy contacts), AverickMedia, InfoGlobalData. Pricing patterns are subscription ($1,500-$6,000/year) or per-contact ($0.10-$0.40). Distinct from our existing 2026-05-16 'licensed-pharmacist-registry' brief — that brief targets individual RPh/PharmD professionals; this brief targets pharmacy BUSINESSES (the dispensing site), which is the buying entity for wholesale, POS, automation, and PBM channels. The CDC and state Boards of Pharmacy maintain public facility registries in all 50 states. Demand is durable because pharmacy facility-level data drives wholesaler account onboarding, PBM credentialing, and automation capex decisions — all of which require the FACILITY's DEA + NABP IDs, not the pharmacist's RPh number.
target_audience: Pharmaceutical wholesalers and distributors (Cardinal Health, AmerisourceBergen/Cencora, McKesson, Morris & Dickson, HD Smith) recruiting independent pharmacy accounts — each facility represents $300K-$2M/year in wholesale GMV; pharmacy management system (PMS) and POS vendors (PioneerRx, BestRx, ComputerRx, Liberty Pharmacy Systems, Micro Merchant Systems, Rx30, Datascan) selling $300-$2,000/month SaaS to independent sites; pharmacy automation and robotics vendors (Parata, ScriptPro, RxSafe, Omnicell, BD Rowa) selling $50K-$500K dispensing systems; PSAO (Pharmacy Services Administrative Organizations like AmerisourceBergen's Elevate Provider Network, McKesson's Health Mart, Cardinal's Leader, IPC, EPIC Pharmacies) recruiting member pharmacies; specialty pharmacy accreditors (URAC, ACHC) prospecting; compounding pharmacy supply (PCCA, Medisca, Letco Medical); pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) for credentialing and network outreach; 340B contract pharmacy program enrollers; pharmacy E&O / professional liability insurance brokers (Pharmacists Mutual); pharmacy financing and acquisition advisors (M&A is hot — corporate chains and PE rollups actively buy independents).
public_data_sources: State Boards of Pharmacy facility license registries (all 50 states + DC, distinct from individual pharmacist licensure)
NABP (National Association of Boards of Pharmacy) e-Profile / Pharmacy Search public lookup
DEA Diversion Control Active Controlled Substance Registrant lookup (public FOIA-released file)
CMS NPPES (Type 2 organizational NPIs filed under pharmacy taxonomy codes 333600000X and subcodes)
CMS Medicare Part D Prescriber and Pharmacy file (Medicare-enrolled pharmacies)
HRSA 340B OPAIS covered entity / contract pharmacy registry
USP <797>/<800> compounding pharmacy accreditation registries (PCAB / ACHC)
State Secretary of State business registry cross-reference for ownership entities
competitive_landscape: Crowded at the premium subscription tier but no flat-file SKU under $200. FrescoData, HealthcareMailing, LeadsPlease, MedicoLeads, BookYourData, AverickMedia, and InfoGlobalData all sell some version of a pharmacy facility list, but pricing is either annual subscription ($1.5K-$6K) or per-contact tiered. None offer a state-by-state one-time CSV under $100. DataStructured wedge: $49-$79 per state CSV of independent (non-chain) pharmacies enriched with NABP + DEA + NPI cross-references — 90%+ cheaper than subscription tier, and explicitly filtered to INDEPENDENTS (CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, Walmart, Kroger excluded by chain-name and corporate-owner filter), which is exactly the segment wholesalers, PSAOs, and automation vendors prospect.
monetization_model: State-level CSVs at $49-$79 each. Fields: pharmacy DBA name, legal entity name, NABP number, DEA registration, NPI (Type 2), street address, phone, owner-of-record name, pharmacist-in-charge, license status, services offered (retail / compounding / specialty / LTC / mail-order), Medicare/Medicaid enrollment flag. Top-5-state bundle (CA + TX + FL + NY + PA) at $199. National independents-only bundle (~19,400 records) at $349 vs. competitor $1,500-$6,000 subscriptions. Add-ons: '340B contract pharmacies only' filter SKU ($99), 'compounding pharmacies only' filter SKU ($99) — both are higher-LTV buyer segments.
estimated_market_size: ~88,000 total US pharmacies (NABP 2025). ~19,400 independent community pharmacies (NCPA). ~7,500 specialty pharmacies. ~5,500 compounding pharmacies (PCAB/ACHC accredited subset is ~600). Top-20 chains own ~40% of all retail dispensing sites — the remaining 60%+ is the addressable independent universe. Buyer LTV by segment: wholesaler account = $300K-$2M/year GMV; PMS software = $3.6K-$24K/year SaaS; automation = $50K-$500K capex one-time; PSAO membership = $2K-$10K/year fees per pharmacy; PBM credentialing services = $5K-$25K/year; pharmacy M&A advisory = $50K-$500K per transaction.
data_freshness_requirement: Semi-annual updates. Pharmacy facility licenses renew annually or biennially. Closures and ownership changes ~6-9% per year (driven by chain-acquisition rollups, PBM reimbursement pressure, and retirements). DEA registration changes flagged via DEA Controlled Substance Registrant file updates.
compliance_notes: PASS. All fields sourced from state pharmacy board public license registries (public record under state pharmacy practice acts), NABP public profile, DEA public registrant lookup (FOIA-released), and CMS NPPES (public per HIPAA — organizational NPI is public). Pharmacist-in-charge name is public per state board records. No patient data, no PHI, no consumer PII. DEA registration numbers are part of the public DEA Diversion Control registrant file. Source attribution per state board URL and DEA/NABP/CMS URLs.
next_steps: Harvest CMS NPPES Type 2 NPIs filtered by pharmacy taxonomy 333600000X (Community/Retail Pharmacy) and subcodes for compounding/specialty/LTC
Cross-reference with DEA Controlled Substance Registrant file to attach DEA numbers and validate active dispensing status
Scrape state board facility license registries for TX, CA, FL, NY, PA (top-5 by pharmacy count) to attach state license number, status, and pharmacist-in-charge

Build chain-exclusion filter: regex against top-30 chain DBA names (CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, Walmart, Kroger, Publix, Costco, Sam's Club, Albertsons, Safeway, H-E-B, Target, Wegmans, etc.) plus corporate-owner entity match
Launch TX independents-only SKU at $49 on Gumroad; outreach via r/pharmacy, LinkedIn pharmacy-owner groups, NCPA member channels, and PMS vendor partner programs (PioneerRx/BestRx)
researcher_notes: This is the FACILITY-level companion to our existing pharmacist-license brief (2026-05-16) — not a duplicate. The buyers are structurally different: pharma wholesalers, PMS vendors, automation OEMs, PSAOs, and PBMs all credential and prospect at the PHARMACY (facility) level, using NABP + DEA + NPI as the keying identifiers. The individual RPh license is not actionable for these buyers. The chain-exclusion filter is the killer feature — every major vendor sells 'pharmacy lists' that are 60-70% chain sites (which are non-prospectable because they're centrally owned by HQ). An independents-only SKU is the exact list every wholesaler rep, PSAO recruiter, and PMS sales team actually wants. Engineering is moderate: NPPES + DEA files are bulk-downloadable, state board harvesting is incremental. Top-5 states captures ~45% of the independent universe. Defensible at $49/state because the cleaning work (chain exclusion + NABP/DEA/NPI cross-reference) is non-trivial and the buyer LTV makes a 100x ROI trivial.
